validation.notes: Ran from the workspace root; the script prints 'regression: durable tool lifecycle invariants hold across effect-gate, execution, progress, drive' and exits 0. It links four real production modules in one VM graph via .prale-eval/subject.mjs createGraph - packages/agent/src/harness/execution/effect-gate.ts, packages/agent/src/harness/execution/tools.ts, packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/progress.ts and packages/agent/src/harness/runtime/drive/tools.ts - and supplies its own boundary fakes for the Session scalar store, the lane mutation line, the emitBatch event bus, the HookRegistry hook bus, the chord context, pi-ai argument validation and tool placement. Only the module-private performToolInvocation is exposed through the subject trailers hook; no production module is stubbed. Coverage: (1) gate semantics - a fresh gate admits, beginAbort alone neither signals nor admits and refuses new effects with the shared AbortRequested, signalAbort aborts the already-admitted signal (listener fires once, reason is AbortRequested); (2) executeToolCall turns synchronous and asynchronous tool throws into isError:true results with the original message, and an abort-first gate never starts the tool; (3) a recovered invocation that emits live-only progress, an explicit checkpoint and another live update observes all three live updates in order tagged recovery:true while the durable pendingToolOutput snapshot goes undefined -> checkpoint -> still checkpoint, and the subsequent throw yields a final message with isError:true and an after_tool hook that sees the error; (4) with the checkpoint commit and the live delivery both held open, after_tool cannot run early, and after release the mutation log order is commit -> after_tool -> publish-outcome, so final publication follows progress drain; (5) an abort signaled after admission reaches the running tool's AbortSignal, the tool's real result is kept (isError:false) and after_tool does not start. Fault detection was checked by restoring each repaired file to its faulty baseline one at a time and all three together: each run fails with an uncaught node:assert/strict assertion ('signalAbort must abort the admitted work's signal', 'a synchronous tool throw must stay an error result', 'a live-only update must never be persisted') rather than crashing, failing to import or timing out. No timers, randomness or external services are used; ordering is controlled with promises. Limitation: the repository's vitest suites could not be executed because no node_modules are installed in the workspace and dependency installation is out of scope, so the same behaviours were asserted directly against the production modules through the VM graph.
